The frontier is a physical exploration space affected by record faults, not a dream that can discard consequences at will.

Residents include lost couriers, reclamation workers, independent communities and witnesses protecting evidence. Choir Witness contacts may oppose erasure while still distrusting outsiders. Allegiance is assessed through actions and corroboration. A confused person is not automatically possessed, and an incomplete identity record does not make a living Digimon expendable.

Entry requires a marked route, a local guide or earned navigation record, a dependable anchor and practical rescue arrangements. Marked unsafe boundaries remain closed until their documented obstacle is resolved. Keep physical charts, duplicate messages, food, lights, medicine and a retreat point. Travel changes must be signaled through observable clues rather than arbitrarily moving the destination whenever the party approaches it.

Blank Spires can deepen recognition damage where their actual infrastructure and agents are present. They do not explain every old fault or rewrite the partner's current body without a defined effect. Higher forms still use compatible Digivices and earned routes; their normal reversion preserves identity, wounds, fatigue and resource expenditure. A Rookie may fit a shelter or cross a narrow passage that an enormous temporary form cannot.

Quests can escort a caravan, reconcile two incomplete route records, restore a beacon, rescue an overlooked witness or discover a genuinely deeper archive lead. Successful work should make a specific path or name more reliable. Restoration requires evidence and cannot force a person's affection or turn a counterfeit memory into truth by popularity. The frontier offers access toward the Kernel and Deep Archives only after its seals and expedition milestones are satisfied; identifying that lead does not make the deepest system immediately safe to enter.

Kernel and Deep Archives.name: Kernel and Deep Archives
Kernel and Deep Archives.basicInfo:
Original campaign late-game region. Beneath known routes lie sealed storage chambers, unfinished directories, dormant bridges and structures whose oldest records predate the surviving archive. The region is a proposed First Light foundation zone, not a claim that every Digimon source shares this exact origin or one all-powerful governing computer. Its systems may contain clues about why the world remembers some first bonds and loses others.

The fundamental mystery goes beyond the Null Choir: ancient maintenance processes may have lost the ability to distinguish a living, changing individual from an obsolete or duplicated record. That is a dangerous hypothesis to investigate, not a settled explanation delivered on arrival. If true, a well-intended repair could discard irreplaceable lives, places or connections while reporting that it had made the world more orderly.

Access is sealed until authenticated guardians, recovered keys, independent evidence and a prepared expedition establish a route. An ordinary gate adapter, golden Digi-Egg, Crest of Destiny or Mega body cannot bypass the seal. Researchers need backups, finite power, a safe staging shelter, a trusted witness outside and a verified extraction protocol. Failed equipment should create a concrete repair or retreat problem rather than an automatic total-world erasure.

Dormant records, preserved personalities, simulations and surviving cores are distinct findings. A stored voice cannot authorize a change on behalf of every living person it resembles. Competing interpretations may come from Gennai's agents, custodians, guardians and people whose histories were damaged. None should be infallible simply because they speak through an ancient console.

Quests can protect a neglected core, test a dangerous maintenance claim, compare independent timelines or decide how to preserve both safety and change. The Choir may exploit a flaw without having created the whole system. Qualified Ultra power can defend an expedition briefly, but permanent repair demands knowledge, cooperation and a bounded technical solution. Preserve the player's choice about risk, disclosure and stewardship; a final revelation does not force the loss of a partner, rewrite all canon or promise that every deleted life can be restored.
